name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $Y=PJ{P}^{-1},$ find ${2}^{Y}.$
worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)={2}^{x}$ and the given matrix $Y,$ we have

$$
{2}^{Y}={2}^{PJ{P}^{-1}}=P\cdot ({2}^{J})\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $J$ is a Jordan block with $1$s on the main diagonal, we have

$$
f(J)=[\begin{aligned}f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) \\ 0 & f(1)\end{aligned}].
$$

The derivative of $f$ is ${f}^{′}(x)={2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ So, we get

$$
{2}^{J}=[\begin{aligned}f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) \\ 0 & f(1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{1} & {2}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0 & {2}^{1}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{2}{1\cdot 1-1\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{Y} & =P\cdot ({2}^{J})\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & -2+4\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-4\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & 8\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ -2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & 2+4\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Consider the following matrices:

Y=[−14−13],J=[1101],P=[2111]

Given that Y=PJP−1, find 2Y.

a
[2−4ln⁡28ln⁡2−2ln⁡22+4ln⁡2]
b
[3−5ln⁡23ln⁡2−3ln⁡25+ln⁡2]
c
[2ln⁡26−2ln⁡2]
d
[ln⁡2−2ln⁡2−ln⁡22ln⁡2]
e
[1511]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Given a function f and matrices A and S, where S is invertible, we have f(SAS−1)=S⋅f(A)⋅S−1.

For f(x)=2x and the given matrix Y, we have

2Y=2PJP−1=P⋅(2J)⋅P−1.

Now, since J is a Jordan block with 1s on the main diagonal, we have

f(J)=[f(1)f′(1)0f(1)].

The derivative of f is f′(x)=2xln⁡x. So, we get

2J=[f(1)f′(1)0f(1)]=[2121ln⁡2021]=[22ln⁡202].

Also, the inverse of P is

P−1=21⋅1−1⋅1[1−1−12]=[1−1−12].

Therefore, we conclude that

2Y=P⋅(2J)⋅P−1=[2111][22ln⁡202][1−1−12]=[2111][2−2ln⁡2−2+4ln⁡2−24]=[2−4ln⁡28ln⁡2−2ln⁡22+4ln⁡2].
